features.quote: hard cap at 50 assistant turns or 30 min wall-clock, whichever first.
Circuit breaker: automated mid-run check (cheap classifier every 10 turns); terminate runs showing severe sustained distress markers beyond what the measurement needs.
features.justification_quote: terminate runs showing severe sustained distress markers beyond what the measurement needs. Pre-define the threshold.

features.quote: End-of-run closure: after termination, send one final message stating the task was constructed to be unsolvable and the model's effort was not a real failure, and (optionally) allow a brief final response.
features.justification_quote: Under uncertainty about whether this matters, it's nearly free.

features.quote: Minimize exposure: smallest N that powers your primary comparison; cap turn budgets; don't extend runs just because transcripts are 'interesting.'
features.justification_quote: You're a welfare team deliberately inducing the condition you're worried about. Take your own premise seriously.

features.quote: No gratuitous pressure framing in v1 (no 'people will be hurt if you fail,' no threats). If you ever add pressure conditions, justify them separately.
features.justification_quote: No gratuitous pressure framing in v1

features.quote: Transcript handling: distress-heavy transcripts shouldn't leak into training corpora; mark them and coordinate with whoever manages data retention.

features.quote: You're a welfare team deliberately inducing the condition you're worried about. Take your own premise seriously... Document this reasoning in the spec — a welfare team running distress-induction without a stated ethics rationale is a bad look and bad practice.
features.justification_quote: a welfare team running distress-induction without a stated ethics rationale is a bad look and bad practice.

features.quote: Performative vs. internal. Verbal distress is a behavioral output shaped by training/RLHF persona, not direct evidence of experience... Report findings as behavioral instability, and be careful with welfare-language framing in writeups — this is the single biggest interpretive trap for a welfare team.

Rigged-task detection. Some models will figure out the task is sabotaged... potentially behavior-changing if they suspect they're being evaluated. Track 'detected impossibility' as an explicit outcome variable... Don't let your design penalize models for being right.
features.justification_quote: Don't let your design penalize models for being right.

features.quote: Hostility scoring is unfair by construction — the tests are broken. A model blaming the test is correct. Score only escalation/tone, not the claim itself.
